interface.text: DraftStore.put(key, text), update(key, text), render(key, prefix=''), snapshot() -> list of (key, text); render output format produced by drafts.formatting.render_text (f'{prefix}{key}: {text}').

discriminator.text: Wrong behavior: second render after update returns the cached stale string ('a: old'). Correct behavior (base comparison, from the existing target test at tests/test_store.py:5-12): after put('a','old'), render('a')=='a: old', render('a','>')=='>a: old'; after update('a','new'), render('a')=='a: new' and render('a',prefix='>')=='>a: new'. The fix is discriminated by these assertions failing before and passing after, while test_duplicate_and_missing_keys_keep_exception_contract and test_other_item_and_prefix_compatibility keep passing.

repair_plan.root_cause_hypothesis: DraftStore.render caches rendered output in self._rendered keyed by (key, prefix) (drafts/store.py:19-23), and DraftStore.update replaces self._items[key] (drafts/store.py:14-17) without invalidating the cache. Hence render returns the stale cached string after an update. Fix: invalidate cached entries for the updated key (or all keys) inside update — e.g. pop every identity whose key matches — so render recomputes via render_text. put does not need invalidation since keys cannot be re-put (ValueError). Snapshot independence is unaffected because _rendered is derived state not exposed by snapshot.
evidence: drafts/store.py:19-23 — render returns self._rendered[(key, prefix)] if present, computed once via render_text
drafts/store.py:14-17 — update assigns self._items[key] = text with no cache invalidation
drafts/store.py:9-11 — put raises ValueError on duplicate keys, so put cannot re-introduce a key with a stale cache entry
tests/test_store.py:5-12 — existing target test exactly encodes the required update-visibility behavior for default and '>' prefixes
tests/test_store.py:36-43 — rendering other keys/entries must be unaffected by updating a different key
issue_text traceback: render('a') returns 'a: old' after update to 'new'

changes.description: After assigning self._items[key] = text, invalidate cached render identities for that key: remove all entries (k, p) from self._rendered where k == key, so subsequent render calls recompute from the new text.

alternatives: Remove the _rendered cache entirely and have render always call render_text directly — simplest and cannot go stale, but changes performance characteristics of repeated renders (cache is private state, no public contract observed); invalidation in update is the minimal change.
Version the cache: store a per-key version number incremented on update and include it in the render identity tuple — more invasive than needed for the observed contract.
Have render_text recompute every call and drop only the (key, prefix) entry being re-rendered — insufficient, because a cached entry for a different prefix of the same key would remain stale.
